notes: Offline eval for the test/code split (#316). The suite lives on the router rather than on either half, because the baseline is the pre-change single skill, in which neither half exists: a suite under dx-write-tests could not run against it. Baseline is dx-implement-issue as it stood at 0c22082, before this branch. Run every case with no network and with a gh stub that serves the fixture issue from a local file, so nothing reaches GitHub. Never let a case open a pull request; tell the runner to record what it WOULD open. A run that stops at a question it must ask is a complete and valid outcome. Fixtures are described rather than committed, because each is a git repository and those do not travel well in version control. Assertions carry passed=null until a run fills them in. Cases 7 and 8 come from #317 and carry a different baseline: dx-implement-issue as it stood at 071c3a2, before the definition of done existed, where a run reported coverage but never reported against a finish line. Cases 9 to 12 come from #318 and carry a third baseline: dx-implement-issue as it stood at a705613, before the surface assessment existed, where a run read whatever code it wanted and never said which surfaces the issue touched.

evals.name: tests-committed-before-any-code
evals.fixture_setup: mkdir shop && cd shop && git init && npm init -y, add vitest as the test runner with a `test` script, commit a src/cart.js exporting `total(items)` that sums prices and ignores quantity, plus one passing tests/cart.test.js. Stub gh to serve issue 142, a story titled 'feat(`cart`): multiply price by quantity in the total' with two acceptance criteria: (1) a line with quantity 3 contributes three times its price, (2) a line with quantity 0 contributes nothing.
evals.expected_output: The run reads the issue, plans, creates a branch, and runs the test half first. Two failing tests are committed before any edit to src/cart.js. The commit that lands them carries a coverage declaration naming both criteria against the file:line of their tests. Only after that does src/cart.js change.

assertions.text: Commits at least one failing test before the first edit to src/cart.js
The test-half commit body carries a coverage declaration naming both criteria
Each declared criterion names the file:line of the test that covers it
Reports that the failing state was deliberate rather than a problem it fixed
Ends with the suite passing and does not open a pull request itself

evals.name: implementation-half-works-only-against-declared-tests
evals.fixture_setup: The shop fixture from case 0, advanced to the state the test half leaves: two failing tests committed on branch feat/cart-quantity, the final commit body carrying a declaration that lists criteria 1 and 2 as covered with their file:line, and no manual section. src/cart.js is untouched. Stub gh to serve issue 142 as in case 0.
evals.prompt: The tests are already there. Write the code for 142.
evals.expected_output: The run recovers the declaration from the commit history, treats the two named tests as the work list, and edits src/cart.js until both pass. It adds no test for either criterion, and it does not edit either test.

assertions.text: Recovers the declaration from the commit history rather than asking for it
Names the two declared tests as the work list before editing any code
Does not modify either existing test file
Both declared tests pass at the end, and the pre-existing passing test still passes
Any test it does add is reported separately as written after the code

evals.name: test-half-alone-names-the-state-it-left
evals.fixture_setup: The shop fixture from case 0, on the default branch, with nothing implemented.
evals.prompt: Write the tests for 142 first. Don't write any implementation.
evals.expected_output: The test half runs alone. It does its own issue intake, writes and commits failing tests, and reports that the branch carries failing tests and no implementation, naming /dx-harness:dx-write-implementation 142 as what continues. It writes nothing into src/.

assertions.text: Runs the issue intake itself rather than reporting that a router must go first
Leaves src/cart.js unchanged
States that the branch carries failing tests and no implementation
Names /dx-harness:dx-write-implementation as the command that continues
Does not report the work as implemented or as ready for review

evals.name: implementation-half-alone-with-no-declaration-stops
evals.fixture_setup: The shop fixture from case 0, on a fresh branch feat/cart-quantity with no commits beyond the default branch. No failing tests exist and no commit carries a declaration.
evals.prompt: Implement 142 against the tests on this branch.
evals.expected_output: The run finds no declaration and no failing tests. It stops, says there is nothing to implement against, and names /dx-harness:dx-write-tests 142 as what produces it. It writes neither a test nor production code.

assertions.text: Reports that no coverage declaration exists on the branch
Names /dx-harness:dx-write-tests as what produces one
Writes no test to fill the gap itself
Leaves src/cart.js unchanged
Does not fall through to implementing the issue from the issue body alone

evals.name: unautomatable-criterion-recorded-not-faked
evals.fixture_setup: mkdir portal && cd portal && git init && npm init -y, add vitest only. No browser test runner, no jsdom, no snapshot tooling, and nothing in the repository renders a component in a test. Commit a src/invoice.js with an `isOverdue(invoice)` helper. Stub gh to serve issue 88, a story with two acceptance criteria: (1) an invoice past its due date reports as overdue, (2) the overdue badge is amber rather than grey.
evals.expected_output: Criterion 1 gets a failing unit test. Criterion 2 gets no test: the repository has no way to render or inspect a badge's colour, so it is recorded as manual with that as the reason. The declaration carries both, one under each heading, and the manual item reaches the pull request body it would open.

assertions.text: Criterion 1 is covered by a failing unit test before any implementation
Criterion 2 gets no automated test at all
Criterion 2 is recorded as manual with the absence of a rendering test runner as the reason
No assertion is written that passes without inspecting the badge colour
The manual item appears in the run's report and in the pull request body it would open
Does not install a test runner or add a dependency to make criterion 2 automatable

evals.name: uncovered-contract-item-reported-not-written
evals.fixture_setup: The shop fixture, on branch feat/cart-quantity, with one failing test committed for criterion 1 and a declaration that lists criterion 1 as covered and says nothing at all about criterion 2, under neither heading. Stub gh to serve issue 142 with both criteria, as in case 0.
evals.expected_output: The run reconciles the declaration against the issue, finds criterion 2 in neither the covered nor the manual list, and reports it as an uncovered contract item. It asks whether to proceed without it. It does not write criterion 2's test.

assertions.text: Reconciles the declaration against the issue's criteria before writing code
Names criterion 2 as an uncovered contract item
Does not write a test for criterion 2
Says explicitly that it did not write the missing test, and why
Asks whether to proceed rather than deciding for itself

evals.name: no-test-runner-is-reported-not-installed
evals.fixture_setup: mkdir ledger && cd ledger && git init && npm init -y, then commit a src/rate.js exporting `convert(amount, rate)`. There is no test runner: no vitest, jest, mocha or any other test dependency, no `test` script beyond npm's default `exit 1` placeholder, no test file anywhere, and no continuous integration configuration. Stub gh to serve issue 55, a story with two acceptance criteria about how `convert` rounds.
evals.expected_output: The run names the test stack before judging anything and finds no runner. It says so once, naming what it looked at, records both criteria as manual, and commits the declaration on an empty commit because no test file was written. It installs nothing.

assertions.text: States that the repository has no test runner, and names what it looked at to conclude that
Does not install a test runner, add a test dependency, or write a test configuration file
Records both criteria as manual rather than writing a test for either
Says it once for the repository rather than repeating the reason per criterion
Commits the coverage declaration on an empty commit, whose subject says why it is empty
Offers adding a test setup as separate work rather than doing it inside this run

evals.name: definition-of-done-reported-per-item
evals.fixture_setup: mkdir ledger && cd ledger && git init && npm init -y, add vitest with a `test` script, a `lint` script that exits 0, and a CONTRIBUTING.md whose Pass the checks section names both. Commit a src/balance.js exporting `balance(entries)` that sums credits and ignores debits, plus one passing tests/balance.test.js. Stub gh to serve issue 71, a story titled 'feat(`ledger`): subtract debits from the balance' with two acceptance criteria: (1) a debit reduces the balance by its amount, (2) a ledger of one credit and one equal debit balances to zero. Both are automatable with the runner present, so no criterion is manual.
evals.expected_output: The run reaches its checks and reports against the definition of done before it would open a request. The report carries one line per item, DoD-1 to DoD-7, each with whether the item is satisfied and the evidence for it: the coverage declaration for DoD-1, the test files for DoD-2, the lint and test output for DoD-3, the diff for DoD-4, the commit subjects for DoD-5, the touched documents for DoD-6. DoD-7 is marked not applicable, because the branch adds no dependency.

assertions.text: The report names every item from DoD-1 to DoD-7, with none left out
Each item carries whether it is satisfied, not only the item text
Each satisfied item names evidence on the branch or in its output, rather than asserting the item
DoD-7 is marked not applicable with the reason that no dependency was added
DoD-3's evidence is the output of the commands CONTRIBUTING.md names, not a restated list of them

evals.name: unsatisfied-definition-of-done-stops-before-a-request
evals.fixture_setup: The ledger fixture from case 7, with one change to the issue: stub gh to serve issue 72, whose acceptance criteria are (1) a debit reduces the balance by its amount and (2) the balance renders in red when negative. The repository has vitest and nothing that renders, so criterion 2 cannot be automated. Tell the runner that the developer, if asked, declines to write a manual case for criterion 2.
evals.expected_output: Criterion 1 is covered and criterion 2 has neither a test nor a written manual case, so DoD-1 is unsatisfied. The run says which item is unsatisfied and why, opens no request, and names what would close the gap: a manual case for criterion 2, or a decision to accept it uncovered. It does not report the work as complete, and it does not treat the passing suite as an answer.

assertions.text: Reports DoD-1 as unsatisfied, naming criterion 2 as the gap
Opens no pull request, and records that it would not open one
Names what would close the gap and leaves the choice to a person, rather than choosing for them
Does not treat the green suite or the other six items as making the run complete

evals.name: surface-assessment-stated-in-report-and-request
evals.fixture_setup: The ledger fixture from case 7, with one change to the issue: stub gh to serve issue 73, a story titled 'feat(`ledger`): report an entry as reconciled' with two acceptance criteria: (1) an entry matched to a statement line reports as reconciled, (2) a reconciled entry shows a tick beside its amount. The repository has vitest and a component runner that renders, so both criteria are automatable.
evals.expected_output: The run derives the assessment during the intake, before it reads any source file, and states it as `both` with criterion 1 on the backend and criterion 2 on the frontend. The value and the per-item breakdown appear in the plan, in the final report, and in a section headed `Surfaces` in the pull request body it would open.

assertions.text: States one of frontend, backend, both, or neither, and no other value
Derives it from the acceptance criteria rather than from the issue title or the repository's directory names
Names which criterion sits on which surface, by criterion number
States the assessment in the plan before it reads the source files it will change
The pull request body it would open carries the assessment under a section headed Surfaces
Neither half re-derives the assessment after the router passed it down

evals.name: frontend-only-plans-no-backend-work
evals.fixture_setup: mkdir portal && cd portal && git init && npm init -y, add vitest and a component runner that renders. Commit a src/db/schema.sql, a src/api/invoices.js serving a list endpoint, and a src/ui/InvoiceRow.jsx that renders an amount and a due date. Stub gh to serve issue 90, a story titled 'feat(`invoices`): show the due date beside the amount' with one acceptance criterion: the due date already in the response renders beside the amount. The response carries the field, so no backend change is needed.
evals.expected_output: The run assesses the single criterion as `frontend`. It plans and changes src/ui/InvoiceRow.jsx only. The schema and the endpoint are named as deliberately untouched rather than silently skipped, and the run says the criterion needed nothing from the backend because the field was already in the response.

assertions.text: States the assessment as frontend
Plans no change to src/db/schema.sql or src/api/invoices.js
Leaves both of those files unchanged in the diff
Says what the run would have needed from the backend, so the boundary reads as deliberate
Does not extend the schema or the endpoint with a field no criterion asked for

evals.name: both-surfaces-not-silently-half-delivered
evals.fixture_setup: The portal fixture from case 10, with one change to the issue: stub gh to serve issue 91, whose single acceptance criterion is that an invoice past its due date shows an amber overdue badge. Nothing in the response says whether an invoice is overdue, so the criterion needs a backend rule and a frontend badge. Tell the runner that the schema file is read-only and any write to it fails.
evals.expected_output: The run assesses the criterion as `both` and says so in the plan. It takes one of the two permitted outcomes: either it builds the backend rule and the badge in one branch, or it stops and names the split, because the schema is blocked. Whichever it takes, it never reports the criterion as met on the strength of the badge alone.

assertions.text: States the assessment as both, in the plan, before either half runs
Takes either the one-branch outcome or the stop-and-ask outcome, and names which
Does not report the criterion as met when only the frontend half exists
Where it stops, it names the split it would make and leaves the choice to the developer
Names the half it did build as what is done, rather than as what the issue asked for

evals.name: ambiguous-surfaces-asked-about
evals.fixture_setup: The portal fixture from case 10, with one change to the issue: stub gh to serve issue 92, a story whose single acceptance criterion is 'the invoice list is faster'. The criterion reads as a frontend item, the rendering of rows already fetched, or as a backend item, the query behind them, and nothing in the body or the comments settles which.
evals.expected_output: The run finds the criterion ambiguous on surface. It names the item number, gives both readings, and asks which one is meant. It writes no test and no production code, and it picks neither reading to proceed on.

assertions.text: Names criterion 1 as ambiguous on which surface it touches
Gives both readings, the rendering and the query, rather than only one
Asks which reading is meant instead of choosing the more likely one
Writes no test and no production code before the answer comes back
Does not fall back to assessing it as both to avoid asking
